claims.text: The baseline is zirconium-alloy cladding with an elemental Cr coating.
Elemental Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
Premature failure of elemental Cr coatings under accident-relevant conditions is caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The elemental Cr coating provides protective performance under either normal-water or accident conditions before failure under combined regimes.
The intervention is to add approximately 5–10 at.% Al to the Cr coating by co-sputtering or a similar method.
Adding 5–10 at.% Al to Cr will produce an in situ duplex Cr2O3–Al2O3 surface scale.
Adding 5–10 at.% Al will refine the Cr(Al) grain structure of the coating.
Al promotes formation of a protective alumina scale with greater high-temperature stability and slower growth than chromia.
The Al2O3 component will impede oxygen ingress into the Cr–Al coating.
The Al2O3 barrier will suppress Cr diffusion into the zirconium substrate.
The duplex oxide scale and refined Cr(Al) microstructure will together limit Cr–Zr interfacial diffusion.
The proposed barrier will delay Cr–Zr interdiffusion and premature coating failure during high-temperature steam exposure.
Relative to pure Cr, the Cr–Al coating will retain improved oxidation resistance in PWR primary water at about 320 °C for up to 60 days.
Relative to pure Cr, the Cr–Al coating will significantly reduce interfacial elemental transport during steam transients around 1200 °C.
The Cr–Al coating will extend overall coating durability across both normal PWR-water and accident-relevant steam regimes.
Al depletion associated with alumina formation can cause structural instability.
The proposed Cr–Al coating may form brittle intermetallic phases that compromise mechanical integrity.

contradictions.description: The initial-state description locates failure under combined normal/accident regimes, whereas the baseline states that premature failure occurs under accident-relevant high-temperature conditions themselves. The applicable failure sequence is therefore not stated consistently.
